concepts.title: Polynomial structure, degree and coefficient slots
concepts.badge_reason: The simulated learner is uncertain about polynomial terminology, missing coefficients and what a zero coefficient means.
assumptions: Integer arithmetic and powers are available.
Polynomial terminology and missing coefficients are not assumed secure.
concepts.jump: Treat coefficients as indexed by exponent slots. A missing written term contributes coefficient 0 without changing the positions of later coefficients.
steps: Fix the exponent slots before reading coefficients.
A polynomial's coefficient is attached to a specific non-negative integer exponent.
power-indexed slots
Classify allowed variable powers.
Real-coefficient polynomials use non-negative integer exponents of x.
polynomial boundary
Insert explicit zero coefficients for missing powers.
Zero preserves the exponent position while contributing no term value.
complete coefficient sequence
Translate back to check the representation.
Reverse translation tests whether each exponent-to-coefficient correspondence was preserved.
same polynomial recovered

misconception.wrong_idea: Missing powers can be deleted from a positional coefficient representation.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: Write all coefficient slots for 2x^4+3x-1, including powers that do not appear.
misconception.repair: Keep every exponent slot. Missing x^3 and x^2 terms have coefficient 0, so the row is 2,0,0,3,-1.

exit.prompt: For 6x^4-x+8, give the degree and the coefficients for powers 4,3,2,1,0, then reconstruct the polynomial.
exit.check: Reading the row back by powers gives the same expression.

anchor.stem: For 2x^4+3x-1, create a coefficient row for powers 4 through 0 and reconstruct the polynomial.
anchor.check: Every source term returns to the same exponent after reverse translation.

concepts.title: Substitute, collect, expand and factor with structure intact
concepts.badge_reason: Basic distribution is demonstrated, but collecting terms and standard identities are uncertain in the simulated preset.
assumptions: Signed-number arithmetic, powers, basic distribution and familiar substitution are available.
Standard identities and collecting polynomial terms are not assumed secure.
concepts.jump: Preserve structure before simplifying: bracket substitutions, align like powers, and expose all products before collecting or applying an identity.
steps: Preserve grouping before computation.
Brackets and aligned powers prevent sign and type errors.
structured expression
Expose every distributive product.
Multiplying two binomials creates one product for each pair of terms.
complete product list
Collect only identical powers.
Only coefficients of the same x^k may be combined.
simplified polynomial
Use inverse expansion as a check.
Factoring and expansion should reconstruct one another under the identity's conditions.
independent algebraic check

misconception.wrong_idea: A binomial square can be formed by squaring only the two visible terms.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: Expand (x+2)(x+2) as four products before combining anything.
misconception.repair: The two cross-products are both 2x, so (x+2)^2=x^2+4x+4.

exit.prompt: Expand (x-2)^2 from a product, then factor x^2-16 and check by multiplication.
exit.check: Multiplying each factor form recovers its expanded polynomial.

anchor.stem: A learner claims (x+2)^2=x^2+4. Expand from the product and identify what was omitted.
anchor.check: At x=1, both the square and corrected expansion equal 9.

concepts.title: Model quantities and justify polynomial identities
concepts.badge_reason: The learner must distinguish a geometric model choice from symbolic manipulation and distinguish universal proof from numerical checking.
assumptions: Universal identity justification and polynomial modelling are not assumed secure.
concepts.jump: Choose the meaning-bearing relation first, then transform it algebraically. For a universal claim, use a law valid for arbitrary x rather than sampled agreement.
steps: Identify the requested quantity or claim type.
Area questions need a geometric relation; every-real-x claims need a universal warrant.
model or proof obligation
Map the givens into the governing relation.
Rectangle sides enter length×width; an identity is transformed symbolically for arbitrary x.
question mapped to relation
Carry out the algebra without changing meaning.
Expansion produces an equivalent polynomial form.
equivalent polynomial
Check units or reversibility.
Square units test the model; reverse factoring checks the identity transformation.
independent consistency check

misconception.wrong_idea: A few matching numerical values are enough to prove a polynomial identity.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: Explain why checking x=0 and x=1 cannot by itself prove two expressions equal for every real x.
misconception.repair: Use a symbolic transformation justified by the distributive law; that warrant applies to arbitrary real x.

exit.prompt: A rectangle has sides x+5 cm and x+2 cm. Write and expand its area, then explain why the product and expansion are equal for every real x.
exit.summary: Area=(x+5)(x+2)=x^2+7x+10 cm^2; distribution establishes the identity for every real x.
exit.check: At x=0 the area is 10 cm^2, consistent with 5×2.

anchor.stem: A rectangle has sides x+4 cm and x+2 cm for x≥0. Model its area, expand it, and state the output unit.
anchor.check: At x=0 the model gives 8 cm^2, matching 4 cm × 2 cm.

concepts.title: Construct a linear polynomial from coefficient and zero constraints
concepts.badge_reason: The simulated learner is uncertain about interpreting a zero and must coordinate two constraints rather than apply one isolated procedure.
assumptions: Substitution into a familiar linear expression and signed-number operations are available.
Interpreting a polynomial zero and coordinating coefficient constraints are not assumed secure.
concepts.jump: Represent all polynomials satisfying the fixed constant first, then turn the specified zero into an equation for the only remaining coefficient; uniqueness follows only after that freedom is exhausted.
steps: Write the constrained family.
A fixed constant b leaves p(x)=ax+b with a as the remaining coefficient for a linear polynomial.
one-parameter family
Translate the zero into an equation.
r is a zero exactly when p(r)=0.
equation ar+b=0
Solve the parameter equation.
Signed-number operations determine the coefficient when r is non-zero.
parameter fixed
Recheck both conditions and remaining freedom.
The constant and zero must both hold; a single forced coefficient establishes uniqueness.
verified unique polynomial

misconception.wrong_idea: Any non-zero scaling preserves both a zero and a fixed constant term.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: If p(x)=ax+6 must have zero 3, does multiplying one solution by 5 keep the constant term equal to 6?
misconception.repair: Scaling preserves zeros but scales the constant too. Use 3a+6=0 to fix a directly.

exit.prompt: Construct a linear polynomial with constant term -4 and zero 2, and justify whether it is unique.
exit.summary: p(x)=2x-4; p(2)=0 and the constant is -4. The coefficient 2 is forced by 2a-4=0, so it is unique.
exit.check: Both constraints hold and the parameter equation has one solution.

anchor.stem: Construct a linear polynomial with constant term 6 and zero 3, then decide whether more than one can satisfy both conditions.
anchor.check: The constant is 6 and p(3)=0; no free coefficient remains.

representations.purpose: Show a changed polynomial as fixed exponent slots so missing powers remain visible without solving Q1 or Q5.

stages.label: Power slots
stages.text: Changed example: 2x^4 - 3x + 5. Make slots 4,3,2,1,0.

stages.label: Place visible terms
stages.text: Attach 2 to power 4, -3 to power 1, and 5 to power 0.

stages.label: Preserve gaps
stages.text: Power-3 and power-2 slots stay present; fill their coefficients yourself.

representations.purpose: Expose the four products in a changed binomial square without giving the supplied Q6 expansion.

stages.label: Whole product
stages.text: Changed example: (x+2)(x+2).

stages.label: Four regions
stages.text: Use x·x, x·2, 2·x, 2·2 as four separate products.

stages.label: Collect later
stages.text: Keep both cross-products visible before combining them.

representations.purpose: Connect changed rectangle side lengths to area and square units without answering Q7.

stages.label: Changed rectangle
stages.text: Sides x+4 cm and x+2 cm.

stages.label: Model choice
stages.text: Area means multiply the two perpendicular side lengths.

stages.label: Unit check
stages.text: cm × cm gives square centimetres; expand only after the model is fixed.

representations.purpose: Show a changed coefficient family and zero condition as linked constraints without supplying Q10's coefficient.

stages.label: Family
stages.text: Changed case: p(x)=a x + 6.

stages.label: Zero condition
stages.text: If the zero is 3, write p(3)=0 before solving.

stages.label: Uniqueness check
stages.text: Ask whether any free coefficient remains after that equation is solved.

representations.purpose: Provide blank positional slots for the supplied polynomial while leaving requested entries to the learner.

stages.label: Supplied powers
stages.text: Powers 3,2,1,0 are fixed columns.

stages.label: Mapping bridge
stages.text: Place each visible term under its matching power; keep the missing slot.

stages.label: Learner work
stages.text: Coefficient cells remain blank, including the x^2 slot.

representations.purpose: Show the supplied product (x+3)(x+3) as four blank multiplication cells so cross-products are visible but unsolved.

stages.label: Two factors
stages.text: The two copies of x+3 are placed on the grid edges.

stages.label: Four products
stages.text: Four cells are visible; no product is evaluated.

stages.label: Learner work
stages.text: Fill all four products before collecting terms.

representations.purpose: Show the supplied rectangle and side labels without expanding or giving its area.

stages.label: Rectangle
stages.text: Length x+3 cm and width x+1 cm.

stages.label: Area cue
stages.text: The perpendicular dimensions are inputs to an area model.

stages.label: Learner work
stages.text: The interior result is left blank for the learner.

representations.purpose: Show fixed constant and zero constraints while leaving the coefficient and uniqueness conclusion blank.

stages.label: Fixed family slot
stages.text: Use p(x)=a x + 2 with coefficient a blank.

stages.label: Zero test slot
stages.text: At x=1 the value must be 0; the equation cell is blank.

stages.label: Learner work
stages.text: Determine a and decide whether any freedom remains.
